title: March Basketball Under the Lottery Reform: Who Rests and Who Plays
brief: Which kinds of teams are likely to rest players, shut down injured players or give young players minutes in March, when our playoffs run? It must explain the expected effect of the anti-tanking lottery reform, teams that do not own their pick, and why late-season numbers from tanking teams should not be trusted.
summary: The experts agree that the new lottery rules should mean fewer tanking teams and fewer March rest days. That is good for our playoffs, which run weeks 19 to 21 and end 2027-03-28. They disagree about teams that do not own their pick. Some say these teams will keep trying to win, others that they may rest veterans or play young players. Expect less late-season chaos than last year, but check every team's pick ownership, seed and roster before the 2027-03-04 trade deadline, and do not draft or bid on March numbers from tanking teams.

paragraphs.text: The experts broadly agree that the new anti-tanking lottery rules will make March more competitive. Fewer teams are expected to tank. One expert counted about eight or nine teams tanking or resting players last season and expects this season's fantasy playoffs to be less extreme. A weak 2027 draft adds to that view. One expert says that under the new rules teams gain nothing real by sitting players late in the season.

The main mechanism is a relegation zone at the bottom. Finishing in the bottom three is now a penalty. With top-protected picks, a bottom-three finish can even give a worse chance at a top-two pick than finishing 4th to 10th. So the worst teams have a reason to win games. One expert names Dallas as a team that may push harder to win for this reason.

Expect win totals to bunch together. Bad teams that used to win about 17 games may now win about 24 because they keep playing their regulars late. Good teams will win fewer games, because there are fewer cheap wins against tanking teams in March. One expert expects every team to keep trying in March and April in this parity era.

This fits our calendar. Two experts say leagues can now end a week later than before, and one suggests a March 28 end for head-to-head playoffs. That is exactly our end date. The late-season injury spike should also be smaller because there should be fewer fake injuries.

sections.heading: Teams that do not own their pick: the experts disagree

paragraphs.text: The experts split on this. One side says these teams have no reason to tank and no downside to losing either. They may rest players, be extra careful with injuries, or give young players development minutes late in the season. The examples named are the Nets, Bucks, Clippers, Pelicans and Mavericks, with Brooklyn and Milwaukee called the main ones to watch. Another note adds that these teams may still lean on young players and protect injured ones. The other side says teams without their own pick have no reason to sit players and will keep pushing to win. They have no reason to finish bottom three, and staying competitive can limit development minutes for their young players. A middle view says they have less reason to fake injuries but may still give young players minutes to see what they have.

For us, the safe reading is that pick ownership alone does not tell you what a team will do. In the auction, do not discount a good player only because his team gave away its pick. Before the 2027-03-04 trade deadline, check where that team sits. A team in the race behaves like a contender. A team clearly out of it, with nothing to gain from winning or losing, is the one that may rest veterans in weeks 19 to 21.

sections.heading: Other teams that may rest or shut down players

paragraphs.text: Reform does not remove every reason to sit players. Teams locked into a seed have no reason to rush injured players back. A deep conference lowers the reward for chasing a top seed, so teams there may rest players more. But one expert notes that a deep conference also removes easy wins against tanking teams, which makes resting riskier. Late in the season, some teams may try to win or lose to land a certain seed or better lottery odds.

A team with no reason to win or lose in March can cut veteran minutes to develop young players. Factor that into what its veterans are worth to you in the playoffs. If a team does decide to tank, injured players may be shut down for the season even when they could have returned. On thin non-playoff teams, an injury to a main player also changes the value of the players left.

Two experts weigh stars on bad teams differently. One says not to worry about tanking when drafting a good player from that team. The other says ranges for stars on bad teams should include the risk of rest and cut minutes, not just per-game value. At the 2026-10-18 auction, a fair middle ground is this. Pay for the star's per-game value, but when two stars are close in price, take the one on a team likely to compete in March. If you own a star on a team that falls out of the race, think about trading him before 2027-03-04.

sections.heading: Young players and rookies in March

paragraphs.text: Rebuilding teams that are not playoff threats give young players more chances because they want to see what they have. Young players on those teams are also fairly safe from random rest days, though injuries can still change things.

Do not plan your playoff roster around a March rookie boom. Two experts say the late-season jump in rookie value may be smaller than usual. Fewer shutdowns by tanking teams means fewer big March minutes for rookies. For our league, that means do not hold a weak rookie on your 2 bench spots all season hoping he breaks out in March. Also, do not spend a large share of your FAB on a rookie just because a team sat a veteran for a few games. Check first that the team is truly out of the race.

sections.heading: Why late-season numbers from tanking teams mislead

paragraphs.text: Players on teams trying to win are easier to trust than players on tanking teams. Tanking teams pull players after three quarters and sit them for much of March. One expert says plainly that March stats from rebuilding teams are hard to trust. Late-season games in general are skewed by tanking.

This matters for draft prep. Last season about eight or nine teams were tanking or resting players. So a young player's big March line from a tanking team was earned with minutes he may not get this year, when fewer teams are expected to tank. A veteran's weak March may simply reflect rest and early benches. Before 2026-10-18, base your prices on full-season or pre-March numbers for players on last year's tanking teams. Do not bid up a young player on the strength of his March line alone.

At the auction, do not discount good players for tank risk alone. Use team context only to break ties between similar stars. Do not pay for March breakouts from last season. Before the trade deadline on 2027-03-04, check four things for each team where you own key players: does it own its pick, is it locked into a seed, is it in a deep conference, and is it clearly out of the race? Players on teams that answer yes to the last three are the most likely to sit during weeks 19 to 21. Trade them to contenders' managers while their value holds. In March, use your 6 weekly acquisitions to stream players from teams still fighting for a seed or trying to escape the bottom three, since those teams have a reason to play their regulars.
